title: Indian Beans (Seam): modeled ₹1,230/qtl left, Pampady → Thrippunithura
summary: September 2021: reported indian Beans (Seam) prices at Pampady and Thrippunithura imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 86% of 21 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹1,230 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 20 same-variety market pairs screened for indian Beans (Seam) in September 2021; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Thrippunithura report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: September 2021
scenes.caption: Pampady (Kerala) and Thrippunithura (Kerala) both reported indian Beans (Seam) prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 21 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Pampady reported a median ₹4,200 per quintal. Thrippunithura reported a median ₹5,400 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,600/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,600 per quintal, and Thrippunithura was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 64 km by road
scenes.caption: 64 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~1 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹14/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹1,107 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹831 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Thrippunithura report, the rule selects 21 of 21 modeled shipping days. 18 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹1,230 per quintal (₹947 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Indian Beans (Seam) route from Pampady to Thrippunithura was positive on 86% of matched days in September 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹123,000, or ₹94,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to indian Beans (Seam)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹14/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Indian Beans (Seam) route from Pampady to Thrippunithura was positive on 86% of matched days in September 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹123,000, or ₹94,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

sources.title: Agmarknet / data.gov.in daily mandi modal prices (retained AGRINET snapshot)
